newsitem.title: INDIA: Scooter bomb kills four near Kashmir leader's home.
newsitem.headline: Scooter bomb kills four near Kashmir leader's home.

text.p: A powerful bomb planted in a scooter taxi exploded near the home of the chief minister of India's troubled Jammu and Kashmir state on Friday, killing four people, police said.
Chief minister Farooq Abdullah was not in the Kashmir Valley at the time, they said.

Jamait-ul-Mujahideen, a militant Kashmiri separatist group, claimed responsibility for the blast which went off about 30 metres (yards) from Abdullah's residence on Gupkar Road in Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir.
One civilian was killed on the spot and three died later in hospital, authorities said.
Police said the bomb, planted inside a three-wheel scooter taxi, exploded near a tea stall on Gupkar Road, a high-security area where at least four members of Abdullah's cabinet live.
A Jamait-ul-Mujahideen spokesman who called local news organisations to claim responsibility said attacks would continue on pro-India leaders in the troubled state.
Abdullah, whose pro-India National Conference party swept state elections in September, escaped several attempts on his life during the campaign.
The blast damaged several houses, two scooter taxis and a security bunker, they said.
"It was a big bang and for the next few moments I was deaf," said 50-year-old Raja Begum, a resident of Gupkar. The blast shattered the windows of her house.
At least 200 people, including women and children, stood outside a police station to identify the bodies.
A vegetable vendor and his brother were among the dead, police said.
The area around the blast site was deserted. There were blood stains on the road and on scattered vegetables.
Police and hospital officials say more than 20,000 people have died in the state, mainly Hindu India's only Moslem-majority province, since the separatist revolt erupted in 1990.
Separatists have intensfied attacks on pro-Indian politicians and paramilitary troops in recent weeks, police officials said.
More than 15 people have been killed in different car, cycle and scooter bomb blasts in Srinagar over the past two months.
On Wednesday, a junior minister in Abdullah's government escaped an attack by separatist guerrillas while he was paying his respects to his deceased father in a cemetery in Srinagar.
On the same day, separatists detonated a powerful bicycle-bomb near Indian military headquarters in Srinagar, injuring two security men and three civilians.
Bashir Ahmad Nengroo, Jammu and Kashmir's Information Minister, condemned Friday's blast.

"The minister said the militants were showing increasing signs of frustration and resorting to killing of innocent civilians. They are visibly unnerved by the growing popularity of the democratic government," an official statement said.
